# Two-sample t-test power analysis
# Design: one-sided pooled t-test, H₁: μ₁ - μ₂ = 4.3 dBA > 0
# Parameters: effect difference = 4.3 dBA, common SD = 7.8 dBA, alpha = 0.05, power = 0.80

# Calculate Cohen's d (standardized effect size)
expected_diff <- 4.3
common_sd <- 7.8
cohens_d <- expected_diff / common_sd

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Expected difference (μ₁ - μ₂):", expected_diff, "dBA\n")
cat("Common SD:", common_sd, "dBA\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Allocation ratio: 1:1\n")
cat("Hypothesis: One-sided (H₁: difference > 0)\n")
cat("α:", 0.05, "\n")
cat("Target power:", 0.80, "\n\n")

# Use power.t.test() for two-sample t-test
# For one-sided test, type = "two.sample", alternative = "one.sided"
# We'll invert to find sample size

library(stats)

# Test a range of sample sizes to find the minimum achieving power >= 0.80
sample_sizes <- seq(10, 150, by = 1)
power_values <- numeric(length(sample_sizes))

for (i in seq_along(sample_sizes)) {
  n <- sample_sizes[i]
  # power.t.test with one-sided alternative
  result <- power.t.test(
    n = n,
    delta = cohens_d,  # effect size in SD units
    sd = 1,             # SD = 1 when using delta in standardized units
    sig.level = 0.05,
    type = "two.sample",
    alternative = "one.sided"
  )
  power_values[i] <- result$power
}

# Create a data frame for inspection
results_df <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = sample_sizes,
  power = power_values
)

# Find minimum n achieving power >= 0.80
min_idx <- which(power_values >= 0.80)[1]
min_n <- sample_sizes[min_idx]
achieved_power <- power_values[min_idx]

# Also check the preceding design
if (min_idx > 1) {
  preceding_n <- sample_sizes[min_idx - 1]
  preceding_power <- power_values[min_idx - 1]
} else {
  preceding_n <- NA
  preceding_power <- NA
}

cat("Sample Size Inversion Results:\n")
cat("=====================================\n")
cat("Minimum n per group achieving ≥80% power:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", round(achieved_power, 4), "\n")
if (!is.na(preceding_n)) {
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", preceding_n, "):", round(preceding_power, 4), "\n")
}
cat("\n")

# Show transition region around the minimum
cat("Power values near transition:\n")
start_idx <- max(1, min_idx - 3)
end_idx <- min(length(sample_sizes), min_idx + 3)
print(results_df[start_idx:end_idx, ])

# Verify with power.t.test() directly
verification <- power.t.test(
  n = min_n,
  delta = cohens_d,
  sd = 1,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("\n\nVerification using power.t.test():\n")
cat("Sample size per group:", verification$n, "\n")
cat("Effect size (Cohen's d):", round(verification$delta, 4), "\n")
cat("Significance level:", verification$sig.level, "\n")
cat("Power:", round(verification$power, 4), "\n")
cat("Alternative:", verification$alternative, "\n")
cat("Type:", verification$type, "\n")

# Final output in requested format
cat("\n\n=== FINAL RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", min_n, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(achieved_power, 4), "\n")
cat("Study design: Two-sample t-test (one-sided)\n")
cat("Allocation: 1:1 (n₁ = n₂ =", min_n, ")\n")
cat("Total N:", 2 * min_n, "participants\n")

# Emit POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(achieved_power, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "preceding_design_sample_size", value = preceding_n, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "preceding_design_power", value = round(preceding_power, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = 2 * min_n, unit = "participants")
  )
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
library(jsonlite)
cat(toJSON(result_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Independent verification of sample size calculation
# Two-sample t-test: one-sided, α=0.05, power=0.80
# Effect size: Cohen's d = 4.3/7.8

library(stats)

# Study parameters
delta_raw <- 4.3  # raw difference in dBA
sigma <- 7.8      # common SD in dBA
cohens_d <- delta_raw / sigma

cat("=== VERIFICATION CALCULATION ===\n\n")
cat("Input parameters:\n")
cat("Expected difference: ", delta_raw, "dBA\n")
cat("Common SD: ", sigma, "dBA\n")
cat("Cohen's d: ", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α): 0.05\n")
cat("Target power: 0.80\n")
cat("Allocation: 1:1 (two-sample)\n")
cat("Alternative: one-sided (H₁: μ₁ - μ₂ > 0)\n\n")

# Method 1: power.t.test() - this is the standard R approach
# Key: when type="two.sample" and alternative="one.sided", we're testing one-sided

cat("METHOD 1: power.t.test() scan\n")
cat("-" * 40, "\n")

power_at_41 <- power.t.test(
  n = 41,
  delta = cohens_d,
  sd = 1,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

power_at_42 <- power.t.test(
  n = 42,
  delta = cohens_d,
  sd = 1,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

power_at_43 <- power.t.test(
  n = 43,
  delta = cohens_d,
  sd = 1,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("Power at n=41: ", round(power_at_41, 6), "\n")
cat("Power at n=42: ", round(power_at_42, 6), "\n")
cat("Power at n=43: ", round(power_at_43, 6), "\n\n")

# Verify minimum design
if (power_at_41 < 0.80 && power_at_42 >= 0.80) {
  cat("✓ n=42 is correct minimum: ", power_at_41, " < 0.80 ≤ ", power_at_42, "\n\n")
  min_n <- 42
} else {
  cat("✗ Unexpected power sequence\n\n")
}

# Method 2: Manual calculation using t-distribution
# For one-sided test at α=0.05, critical value is z_α
# Power = P(Z > z_α - δ√n) where δ = effect size, n = sample size per group

cat("METHOD 2: Manual calculation using normal approximation\n")
cat("-" * 40, "\n")

alpha <- 0.05
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha)  # Upper-tail critical value for one-sided test

cat("Critical value (z_α) for one-sided α=0.05: ", round(z_alpha, 4), "\n")

# Noncentrality parameter: λ = δ√(n/2) for two-sample with 1:1 allocation
# Total sample size = 2n, but for t-test power calculation, we use n per group
# λ = δ√n for two-sample t-test (degrees of freedom approximation)

for (n_test in c(40, 41, 42, 43)) {
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- cohens_d * sqrt(n_test)
  
  # Power ≈ P(t_ν > z_α - λ) where ν = 2n-2 is degrees of freedom
  # Using normal approximation: power ≈ Φ(λ - z_α)
  power_normal_approx <- pnorm(lambda - z_alpha)
  
  # More accurate: use t-distribution
  # Under H1, t-statistic ~ noncentral t with λ and df = 2n-2
  df <- 2 * n_test - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)  # Critical value from t-distribution
  power_exact <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda)
  
  cat("n = ", n_test, ": λ = ", round(lambda, 4), 
      ", power (normal approx) = ", round(power_normal_approx, 6),
      ", power (t-dist exact) = ", round(power_exact, 6), "\n")
}

cat("\n")

# Method 3: Analytical formula
# For large n, power ≈ Φ(δ√n - z_α) where Φ is standard normal CDF
cat("METHOD 3: Analytical verification at minimum design\n")
cat("-" * 40, "\n")

n_min <- 42
lambda_min <- cohens_d * sqrt(n_min)
df_min <- 2 * n_min - 2
t_crit_min <- qt(1 - alpha, df_min)
power_analytical <- 1 - pt(t_crit_min, df_min, ncp = lambda_min)

cat("At n = 42:\n")
cat("  Noncentrality parameter (λ): ", round(lambda_min, 6), "\n")
cat("  Degrees of freedom: ", df_min, "\n")
cat("  Critical t-value: ", round(t_crit_min, 6), "\n")
cat("  Power (noncentral t): ", round(power_analytical, 6), "\n")
cat("  Power (power.t.test): ", round(power_at_42, 6), "\n")
cat("  Match: ", abs(power_analytical - power_at_42) < 0.0001, "\n\n")

  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size_verification", value = 42, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power_at_42", value = round(power_at_42, 6), unit = "proportion"),

  )
), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)

    n = n_test,
    delta = cohens_d,
    sd = 1,

    type = "two.sample",
    alternative = "one.sided"

# Two-sample t-test power analysis
# Design: one-sided pooled t-test, H₁: μ₁ - μ₂ = 4.3 dBA > 0

common_sd <- 7.8
cohens_d <- expected_diff / common_sd

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Expected difference (μ₁ - μ₂):", expected_diff, "dBA\n")

cat("Hypothesis: One-sided (H₁: difference > 0)\n")
cat("α:", 0.05, "\n")
cat("Target power:", 0.80, "\n\n")

# Use power.t.test() for two-sample t-test
# For one-sided test, type = "two.sample", alternative = "one.sided"
# We'll invert to find sample size

# Test a range of sample sizes to find the minimum achieving power >= 0.80

power_values <- numeric(length(sample_sizes))

for (i in seq_along(sample_sizes)) {
  n <- sample_sizes[i]
  # power.t.test with one-sided alternative
  result <- power.t.test(
    n = n,
    delta = cohens_d,  # effect size in SD units
    sd = 1,             # SD = 1 when using delta in standardized units
    sig.level = 0.05,
    type = "two.sample",
    alternative = "one.sided"
  )
  power_values[i] <- result$power
}

# Create a data frame for inspection

  n_per_group = sample_sizes,
  power = power_values
)
